summary: BBN proposes redefining IMP-to-Host error message types and adding new ones so hosts can choose better recovery actions. It includes a new message for when the IMP dropped its ready line, and invites objections before the change.

plainLanguage.summary: BBN proposes changing IMP-to-Host error messages so a Host can better understand what went wrong. The RFC describes several message types and asks for objections before planned installation.

subtitle: A proposal for clearer IMP-to-Host error messages and a Ready Line notice.

tldr.problem: The existing IMP-to-Host error messages did not always give Hosts enough information to choose a recovery action.
tldr.mechanism: The proposal redefines types 1 and 8, adds specific error types 10 through 12, and adds type 13 to report a dropped Ready Line.
tldr.outcome: BBN planned to install the changes within a few months and asked for strong negative comments promptly; the RFC does not report the final result.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 312 as Unknown and records no RFC that updates or obsoletes it. The text describes a proposal and does not say whether it was installed.

sections.title: The Proposed Error Changes
sections.content:
BBN is considering redefining IMP-to-Host error message types 1 and 8 and creating additional types. The stated goal is to help Hosts choose recovery actions without causing serious reprogramming problems.

BBN planned installation within a few months and asked to hear strong negative reactions relatively quickly.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal changes how an IMP reports transmission problems to a Host. BBN asks implementers to raise serious objections soon.

sections.title: A Ready Line Notification
sections.content:
When a Host has not accepted queued input for a long time, an IMP may drop its Ready Line briefly, setting an error flip-flop, then send NOPs and resume normal operation. The proposal adds message type 13 to report that the Ready Line was dropped and the error flip-flop was set.

Type 13 also tells the Host that the IMP will respond to the next completed Host-to-IMP message with type 1 or type 8.
sections.plainLanguage: A new message would tell a Host that the IMP briefly dropped its Ready Line. It would also warn that an error response will follow the Host's next completed message.

sections.title: Specific Error Types
sections.content:
Type 1 would mean the error flip-flop was set on a message the IMP cannot identify. Type 8 would mean it was set while receiving a message identified by the source and link number bits.

New type 10 reports a message too short to identify. Type 11 reports a message too long and includes source and link number. Type 12 reports an illegal message type code, identifies the message with source and link number, and does not include the erroneous type code itself.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal separates unidentified, too-short, too-long and illegal-type errors. Where possible, the error message identifies the source and link number of the original message.

items.label: Unidentified message error
items.desc: Error flip-flop set on a message the IMP cannot identify (redefined).

items.label: Identified message error
items.desc: Error flip-flop set while receiving an identified message (redefined).

items.label: Too short
items.desc: Host-to-IMP message too short to identify (new).

items.label: Ready Line dropped
items.desc: Reports that the Ready Line was dropped and the error flip-flop set (new).
